name: RenormCFG (Lumina2, core)
plain: Lumina's CFG: it splits off extra output channels, applies CFG only only below a sigma limit (cfg_trunc), and caps the norm of the result relative to the positive. At or above the truncation value, which is compared with sigma, it returns the positive only (the negative still costs a pass).
math:
σ<cfg_trunc: e = u + s(c−u) on the first in_channels; ‖e‖≥ρ‖c‖ → e ← e·ρ‖c‖/‖e‖ (when ρ>0)
σ≥cfg_trunc: e = c
result channels = cat(e, cond's extra channels)
label: from code
surprise: Comparison t<cfg_trunc is on the raw timestep arg, which at this point is sigma-scale, so cfg_trunc units depend on the model sampling (inference).

audit.note: comfy/samplers.py:594: cfg_function passes the sampler sigma as args['timestep'], so nodes_lumina2.py:33 compares sigma with cfg_trunc, not a model timestep or time. Also the inputs here are x0 predictions, despite the _eps names.
